title: Vocoder
description: Makes one sound speak with another: the voice on the modulator input is split into frequency bands and the loudness of every band sets the loudness of the same band of the carrier (a chord, a pad, a saw), so the carrier says the words. Consonants such as s and t come from noise that follows the highest band of the voice. For robot voices and the classic Daft Punk sound.

inputs.name: modulator
inputs.title: Voice
inputs.description: The voice (or a rhythm) that does the talking: it only sets the loudness per band.

inputs.name: carrier
inputs.title: Carrier
inputs.description: The sound that speaks: a chord or a pad with many harmonics (a sawtooth, a string, a Delay Llama) works best.

parameters.name: bands
parameters.doc: How many frequency bands: more is clearer speech, fewer is a rougher robot.

parameters.name: attack
parameters.doc: How fast a band follows the voice getting louder.

parameters.name: release
parameters.doc: How fast a band lets go when the voice gets quieter: short is crisp, long is smooth.

parameters.name: width
parameters.doc: The width of a band: 100% just touches the next, 200% overlaps a lot (smoother, less clear).

parameters.name: sibilance
parameters.doc: How much noise follows the highest band of the voice, so s, f and t stay clear.

parameters.name: shift
parameters.doc: Moves the bands of the carrier against those of the voice in semitones: up is a smaller robot, down a bigger one.

parameters.name: mix
parameters.doc: 0% is the carrier as it is, 100% is the vocoded sound.

parameters.name: gain
parameters.doc: The level relative to the carrier (the result is matched to its level).
